goal: Let the quality books say how long each merged pull request was open and where the time went (CI running, rework, waiting for a person to merge), so the weekly brief can say whether CI or people hold pull requests (roadmap R44, unit 1).
changed: quality.py gains an optional, append-only book, books/pulls.csv: one row per merged pull request with its opened, ready and head-CI-finished times, CI time, wait-to-merge time, commit, check and force-push counts, and its pull request link. Without the file every command behaves as before.

fetch, once the book exists, lists each watched repo's merged pull requests since the last one booked (a local-ci repo too), reads their commits, check runs, commit statuses and timeline, and writes pulls/<number>.json; a pull request that cannot be read fails only itself. ingest books each once and never changes a row; summary adds repos.<repo>.pulls with p50 and p95 of open, CI, rework and wait time, never a summed share.
SKILL.md gains The pulls book, with the bucket rule and where it is blind.

claims.claim: The bucket arithmetic (overlap, clipping at the merge, a check that ends after the merge, a check or status that starts after it, every attempt of a re-run check, a trailing pending, no checks, draft then ready, a superseded run still running), fetch, ingest (book, unchanged, reject), check, summary p50 and p95 and null, append-only, and a local-ci repo behave as the SKILL.md says; a pull request link is refused in every other book.
claims.check: tests/test_quality_pulls.py, 45 tests through the fake gh; make test, 1378 tests, 24 skipped, OK
claims.remaining: The fake gh, not GitHub, for the tests.

claims.claim: Against GitHub, fetch read 28 merged pull requests of a public repo, ingest booked them, a second ingest booked none, check passed, and three rows (one simple, one draft that turned ready after its CI, one with seven commits and a four-hour wait) match a hand recomputation from the raw API answers to the second.
claims.check: quality.py fetch, ingest twice, check and summary on a scratch copy of the books; gh api calls for the three pull requests
claims.remaining: Commits dropped by a force push are not listed, so their checks are missed (force_pushes says when).

claims.claim: Booked rows match an independent prototype's per pull request numbers: for all 59 pull requests merged in lyddonb/agent-kit since 2026-11-17, ci and wait agree to the second.
claims.check: quality.py fetch --since 2026-11-17 on a scratch copy of the books watching agent-kit only, compared with a separate prototype script reading the same API
claims.remaining: One public repo; a local-ci repo's statuses are covered by tests only.

claims.claim: Books without books/pulls.csv give the same bytes from check, summary (text, json, public-only), ingest and leak-check as the script at origin/main.
claims.check: both scripts run on one scratch books folder with every optional book except pulls; outputs compared with cmp
claims.remaining: fetch without the file is held by a test that fixes its calls and output, not compared byte for byte against the old script.

next.item: R44 unit 2: in the quality books repo, move the checker pin, create books/pulls.csv, backfill, and add the table to briefs/TEMPLATE.md
next.why_now: Nothing is booked until the books have the file and the pin moves to this version.
next.impact: The weekly brief cannot say whether CI or people hold pull requests until then.
